description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event for non-racing cars. Rear-wheel drives, particularly front engine/rear-wheel layouts, are recommended for the event. The trick to attaining high scores is in how you drive the second section. After switching directions, the section continues into a right hand corner. For the best results you'll want to drift to the left to enter in a straight line, then swing back and exit at full throttle. To balance your car, a large amount of camber is recommended. Try starting your settings at around 5 degrees for both front and back and find a good balance.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event for non-racing cars with 500PP or less. The dirt track will give 4WD cars an advantage, and installation of rally suspension is recommended. To attain good lap times, you'll want to minimise unnecessary 'flashy' drifting, and gain as much traction as possible to move the car forward. When you do drift you will want to keep the drift angle as small as you can. Be careful at the final jumping spot as it can upset the car's balance!

If you exceed the PP limit with power tuning, we recommend adjusting weight balance by adding ballast weight. This stage is rather simple but you won't be able to clear the tight first section with a clean drift if you over-speed, or are lacking speed. Watch for the wall while drifting and keep the car under control with the throttle.

Harden your suspension to ensure stability and handling response. The long first section will have the biggest effect on your score. You'll want to keep drifting as long as you can, but you could also divide the drift as you find necessary. From the 2nd Section onwards, drift while maintaining the driving line.
